nanette-diaz-barragan.text: 'Healthcare is a fundamental right'; has consistently supported the Affordable Care Act and pledges to 'fight to preserve and strengthen health care reforms that make quality, affordable health coverage accessible to all.'
Voted NO on House Republicans' September 2025 spending bill because it 'does nothing to solve the continuing health care crisis.'

source.title: Congresswoman Barragan's Statement on Her Vote on House Republicans' Spending Bill

nanette-diaz-barragan.text: After a May 2026 oversight visit to the Dilley detention center: 'Why are young children being locked up at the Dilley Detention Center...? Our immigrant families should not be treated in this way.'

source.title: Reps. Barragan, Castro, and Stanton Inspect Dilley Trailer Prison

nanette-diaz-barragan.text: Co-led a letter signed by 26 members urging DHS and ICE to investigate CoreCivic for denying people with disabilities basic medical care at the California City immigration facility (Jan. 2026).

source.title: Barragan and Chu Lead California Member Letter on CoreCivic

nanette-diaz-barragan.text: Led 38 lawmakers in a May 2026 letter urging EPA not to weaken the 2024 chemical accident prevention rule: 'All communities deserve to live their daily lives free from toxic exposure.'

source.title: Barragan Leads Bicameral Opposition to New EPA Rule

nanette-diaz-barragan.text: Introduced the Housing Tariff Exclusion Act (H.R. 10416, Sept. 16, 2026), creating a process to exempt home-building materials from current and future tariffs to lower construction costs.

source.title: New legislation would exempt building materials from tariffs

genevieve-angel.text: Priorities include 'lowering out-of-pocket costs, expanding access to care, and improving system efficiency' in health care.
Frames her agenda around 'economic affordability: lowering the cost of living, supporting working families, and expanding economic opportunity.'

Supports 'smart regulation' but says climate initiatives have 'burdened working Americans and increased the cost of living'; says over-regulation of oil, gas and refineries 'worsened economic conditions.'
Calls for 'securing the border, creating fair legal pathways' and 'immigration policies that work in practice.'
Supports the Second Amendment and 'an individual right to own firearms for self-defense, hunting, and sport.'

Describes herself as 'personally pro-life' but respects states' right to decide; opposes a federal pro-life mandate; supports exceptions for the mother's life, rape and incest; opposes taxpayer funding for Planned Parenthood.
States that 'marriage is a union of one man and one woman' and that biological males should not participate in women's sports.
Supports eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and 'giving control back to states, local school boards, and parents.'
Supports requiring 'photo identification and proof of citizenship to vote in federal elections.'
Supports term limits for Congress and restricting lawmakers and families from trading individual stocks.
Endorsed by the California Republican Party and the Los Angeles County GOP.

notes: Angel's campaign site lists only four slogan-level priorities (affordability, public safety, healthcare reform, immigration reform) with no detail; most positions come from her questionnaire answers as summarized on smarter.vote. Ballotpedia could not be retrieved. Barragan's housing and safer-communities issue pages returned 404/limited content; govtrack and legisletter vote data were blocked or generic, so no specific roll-call votes beyond the Sept. 2025 spending bill are recorded.
